text:
maria: Heads-up, seeing a 3x retry spike and really lopsided endpoint hit counts for svc/gpu-infer in us-west-2a starting ~2145006700. grafana: https://graf.redwood/g/p/12345/svc-gpu-infer -> purple line (retries) went vertical. Pods in az-a are saturated while others are idle.
aj: Can you paste the service/endpoint distribution? ipvs+conntrack looks likely.
maria: ipvsadm -Ln output:
```
TCP 10.0.120.77:443 rr
  -> 10.2.11.8:8443 masq 1
  -> 10.2.11.9:8443 masq 1
  -> 10.2.12.3:8443 masq 15  <-- this one getting almost all hits
```
Also `kubectl get endpoints gpu-infer -o wide` shows even endpoints. conntrack stats show half-open/timeouts incrementing on nodes in az-a.
sara: Any recent infra rollouts? mtu, kernel, or network-policy changes?
liam: We had a small kernel bump (5.15.0-rc1 -> 5.15.0) on a subset of nodes in us-west-2a yesterday evening for RDMA perf tests.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: kernel-rollout-worker-group completed on 12 nodes at 2144999000
aj: Kernel bumps + RDMA + mixed MTU is a classic. Any evidence of fragmentation or GSO/TCP segmentation issues?
maria: tcpdump on node 10.2.12.3 shows lots of retransmits and ICMP fragmentation-needed from the ToR. snippet: `IP (frag) 10.0.2.3 > 10.0.2.8: ...` and dmesg: `ske->gso_size mismatch` and `mlx5: rxe: mtu mismatch` entries.
liam: That mlx5 message suggests inconsistent MTU/SG settings for SR-IOV/RDMA. Some hosts are on 9000, others 1500 after the kernel roll. IPVS session affinity/hash can get skewed when packets are dropped before NAT reply reaches client -> effective stickiness to one endpoint.
aj: Quick check: `ip link show` on a healthy vs bad node?
maria: Good node: `eth0 mtu 9000`  Bad node: `eth0 mtu 1500`. Oof.
sara: How did that happen? cloud-init change? ENI plugin? Which nodes are different?
liam: The kernel rollout script re-applied an older NIC driver that reset MTU to 1500 as part of init. Only the kernel-rolled nodes reverted.
aj: Ok plan: disable GSO/TSO/GRO on affected nodes and restart kube-proxy so IPVS sessions rebuild, then roll MTU fix. Commands to run (one-liners):
```
ssh node && sudo ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off
sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 9000
sudo systemctl restart kube-proxy
```
maria: Ran ethtool + mtu set on three worst nodes, restarted kube-proxy. Immediate drop in retries on those nodes. grafana already trending down.
infra-bot: k8s-event: kube-proxy restarted on node-az-a-3 at 2145008320
aj: We'll need to patch the rollout automation to preserve NIC config. Also confirm conntrack cleanup: `conntrack -L | grep 10.0.120.77 | wc -l` should drop after restart.
liam: Also check RDMA stack: ensure that mlx5 driver is same across fleet. We've got a mismatch in dkms modules between kernel packages. I'll push a staging fix to unify the driver package.
sara: Cost/impact note: the retry spike did ~120k extra requests to Dedicated GPU pools over 2 hours -> ~$3200 estimated incremental cost. Filing a post-incident finance note.
maria: Opening a short RCA PR with timeline and remediation steps. Immediate action items: 1) revert kernel change on remaining nodes or reapply correct NIC driver, 2) ensure rollout automation preserves MTU and offload settings, 3) add MTU/driver check to preflight for kernel-rollouts, 4) add an alert for endpoint entropy where one endpoint > 4x median for >5m.
aj: Agreed. Also add a temporary mitigation playbook entry: if ipvs imbalance with retransmits -> check MTU/drivers -> ethtool + restart kube-proxy -> schedule driver fix.
liam: I'll prepare the driver package and coordinate a controlled rollout across us-west-2 tomorrow morning with canary=2 nodes.
sara: Thanks team. Maria, can you paste a short summary for the incident channel once the RCA is in the PR?
maria: Will do. TL;DR: kernel driver change reset MTU on subset of nodes causing fragmentation and IPVS endpoint skew -> ethtool+mtu+kube-proxy restart fixed hot endpoints -> driver unification + automation hardening planned. :white_check_mark:
